summary: An interface can be too narrow, turning simple local calls into opaque, chatty, or inflexible protocols.

points.text: A single high-level operation may accumulate flags and hidden policy, becoming harder to predict than several orthogonal primitives.
Over-encapsulation can prevent efficient batching, diagnostics, and specialized use cases, pushing consumers toward unsupported escape hatches or duplicated logic.
Hiding all implementation context makes failures difficult to diagnose. Stable error types, evidence, observability, and recovery controls are part of the public contract even if they enlarge it.
Prematurely freezing a small interface can lock in the wrong abstraction. During discovery, a wider experimental surface with clear instability markers may support better learning.
